title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let M be an abelian group and fix i. A family (ξ_k)_{k≥N} in M satisfies linear compatibility conditions (1)_k; these are stated on an earlier page not seen here. Grothendieck's notation is C_{h,l} = (h+l)!/(h! l!), so c_{i,k-i} = binom(k,i).

Probable form of (1). Lemma 1.1 on the next page compares c_{j'-j,j} with c_{j'-j,j+i}, where j = k−i and j' = k'−i. So (1) is very probably c_{j'-j,j} ξ_{k'} = c_{j'-j,j+i} ξ_k, that is binom(k'−i, k−i) ξ_{k'} = binom(k',k) ξ_k. This is exactly the relation satisfied by ξ_k = binom(k,i) ξ, because of the identity binom(k',k) binom(k,i) = binom(k',i) binom(k'−i, k−i).

Theorem being proved. If (ξ_k) satisfies (1), there is a unique ξ ∈ M with ξ_k = binom(k,i) ξ for all k ≥ N. In words: a compatible family of 'divided-power-type' multiples comes from a single element. This is the kind of lemma needed when working with divided power polynomial algebras and their de Rham complex, where the products γ_a·γ_b = binom(a+b,a) γ_{a+b} force exactly such binomial relations.

Previous page: reduction to the local case. One reduces to M a Z_(p)-module; Grothendieck writes Z_p for the localization Z_(p), not the p-adics. The coefficients binom(k,i) for k ≥ N have no common prime factor, so a Bezout combination Σ m_α binom(k_α,i) = 1 gives uniqueness. Existence is then checked after the injective map M → ∏_p M_(p).

This page: the case where M is a Z_(p)-module.
(a) Take j = k − i = p^ε with p^ε > i. Then binom(i+p^ε, i) ≡ 1 mod p, either by Lucas or directly. So there are arbitrarily large k with binom(k,i) a unit.
(b) Uniqueness: for such an h_0, necessarily ξ = binom(h_0,i)^{-1} ξ_{h_0}.
(c) Existence: put ξ'_k = binom(k,i) ξ with this ξ. Then (ξ'_k) satisfies (1) by the binomial identity, and ξ'_{h_0} = ξ_{h_0}. Since (1) is linear, η_k = ξ'_k − ξ_k satisfies (1) and η_{h_0} = 0.
(d) This reduces everything to a Corollary: if (ξ_k) satisfies (1) and ξ_{h_0} = 0 for some h_0 ≥ N with binom(h_0,i) ≢ 0 mod p, then ξ_k = 0 for all k ≥ N.

The next page proves the Corollary via Lemma 1.1, which propagates vanishing between indices k, k' using p-adic valuations of the binomial coefficients.
errors: On the previous page Grothendieck writes C_{k,k-i} (e.g. 'C_{k,k-i} ∈ Z_p^*', 'Σ m_α C_{k_α,k_α-i}'); with his convention this should be C_{i,k-i} = binom(k,i). It is a notational slip, as this page uses the correct c_{i,k-i}.
The label (2) is reused: once for the conclusion of the theorem, once for the hypothesis c_{i,h_0-i} ≢ 0 (p) in the Corollary. This is harmless.
'Z_p' means the localization Z_(p), not the p-adic integers; the argument is correct with that reading.
No mathematical gap on this page: the Lucas-type congruence binom(i+p^ε, i) ≡ 1 (p) for p^ε > i is correct, and the reduction to the Corollary is valid because (1) is linear.

ideas.what: Choosing k = i + p^ε with p^ε > i so that binom(k,i) is a p-adic unit, giving arbitrarily large such k
Characterizing families ξ_k satisfying binomial compatibility relations as ξ_k = binom(k,i) ξ, via a local-global reduction (Bezout, then localization at each prime)
ideas.modern_name: elementary lemma on divided-power / binomial relations (as in computing PD de Rham complexes)

ideas.what: Reducing existence to a vanishing statement by subtracting a particular solution, using linearity of the conditions

deep.surprise_reason: Routine elementary number-theoretic step (a Lucas-type congruence, then reduction to a vanishing corollary) inside a technical lemma for the divided power de Rham complex; nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Considérons donc le système des ... ξ'_k = c_{i,k-i} ξ': the ξ here is the one just defined, ξ = c_{i,h_0-i}^{-1} ξ_{h_0}; the transcription is accurate.
On the previous page, 'C_{k,k-i}' should read C_{i,k-i}. This is Grothendieck's slip and is faithfully transcribed, but it should be noted.
'satisfait encore (1)': the parenthesis reading '(1)' is correct; the struck 'les' before (η_k) is fine.
In the reduction sentence 'Donc on est ramené au Corollaire', the word 'au' is written on the next line before 'Corollaire'.
